div.head: VI As 10
div.ab: Teoðe, þæt þa witan ealle sealdan heora wedd ealle togædere þam arcebiscope æt Þunresfelda, þa Ælfeah Stybb ⁊ Brihtnoð Oddan sunu cóman togeanes þam gemote þæs cinges worde, þæt ælc gerefa náme þæt wedd on his agenre scire, þæt hi ealle þæt frið swa healdan woldan, swa Æþelstan cyng hit geræd hæfð ⁊ his witan ǽrest æt Gréatanléa ⁊ eft æt Exanceastre ⁊ syððan æt Fæfresham ⁊ feorðan syððe æt Þunresfelda beforan þam arcebiscope ⁊ eallum þam bisceopan ⁊ his witum, þe se cyng silf namode, þe þæron wæron, þæt man þas domas healdan sceoldan, þe on þissum gemote gesette wæron, buton þam þe þær ær ofadóne wæron: þæt wæs Sunnandæges cyping, ⁊ þæt man mid fulre gewitnesse ⁊ getreowre moste ceapian butan porte.

Decimum, quod sapientes omnes dederunt uadium suum insimul archiepiscopo apud Þunresfeldam, quando Ælfeach Stybb et Brihtnodus Odonis filius uenerunt ad concilium ex uerbo (ore) regis, ut omnis prepositus uadium capiat in suo comitatu de pace seruanda, sicut Æþelstanus rex hoc consuluit et sapientes sui prius apud Grateleiam et postea Exonie et postea apud Fefresham et quarta uice apud Þunresfeldam coram archiepiscopo et episcopis et sapientibus, quos rex ipse nominauit, qui interfuerunt, ut iudicia conseruarentur, que in hoc concilio fuerant instituta, preter hoc quod ante erat (fuit) exceptum: id est negotiatio dominice diei, et quod pleno testimonio et credibili possit emi extra portum.

Teoðe: Þæt þa witan ealle sealdan heora wedd ealle togædere þam arcebiscope æt Þunresfelda, þa Ælfeah Stybb ⁊ Brihtnoð Oddan sunu cóman togeanes þam gemote þæs cinges worde, þæt ælc gerefa náme þæt wedd on his agenre scire, þæt hi ealle þæt frið swa healdan woldan, swa Æþelstan cyng hit geræd hæfð ⁊ his witan ǽrest æt Gréatanléa ⁊ eft æt Exanceastre ⁊ syððan æt Fæfresham ⁊ feorðan syððe æt Þunresfelda beforan þam arcebiscope ⁊ eallum þam bisceopan ⁊ his witum, þe se cyng silf namode, þe þæron wæron, þæt man þas domas healdan sceoldan, þe on þissum gemote gesette wæron, buton þam þe þær ær ofadóne wæron; þæt wæs Sunnandæges cyping, ⁊ þæt man mid fulre gewitnesse ⁊ getreowre moste ceapian butan porte.

Zehntens, dass alle Witan ihr rechtsförmliches Versprechen allesammt dem Erzbischofe zu Thundersfield gegeben haben — als Aelfeah Stybb und Brihtnoth, Oddas Sohn, im Auftrage des Königs jener Versammlung entgegen kamen —, [daraufhin] dass jeder [Grafschafts]vogt in seiner eigenen Grafschaft folgendes rechtsförmliche Versprechen [den Eingesessenen] abnehmen werde: dass sie alle die Friedensordnung so bewahren wollen, wie König Aethelstan es verordnet hat mit seinen Witan zuerst zu Greatley — und wiederum zu Exeter und dann zu Feversham und zum vierten Male zu Thundersfield — vor dem Erzbischofe und allen Bischöfen und seinen Witan, welche der König selbst ernannt hatte, die dabei waren, dass man diese Gesetze halten solle, welche auf jener [frühesten] Versammlung festgesetzt wurden, ausser denen, die davon bereits abgeschafft wurden: nämlich [wieder erlaubt ist] Kaufhandel am Sonntag, und dass man unter vollem und glaubwürdigem Zeugnisse [auch] ausserhalb einer Stadt handeln darf.

Tenthly, that all the witan gave their formal pledge all together to the archbishop at Thundersfield — when Ælfheah Stybb [i.e. ‘stump’ or ‘stock’] and Brihtnoth, Odda's son, came to meet that assembly at the king's command —, [to the effect] that every [shire-]reeve should take the following formal pledge [from the inhabitants] in his own shire: that they would all keep the peace-ordinance as King Æthelstan has ordained it with his witan, first at Greatley — and again at Exeter and then at Faversham and the fourth time at Thundersfield — before the archbishop and all the bishops and his witan, whom the king himself had named, who were present, that those laws should be kept which were established at that [first] assembly, except those that have already been abolished from it: namely, [trade is again permitted] on Sunday, and one may trade [even] outside a town with full and trustworthy witness.

Tenth: The councillors, all in a body, gave their solemn pledges to the archbishop at Thundersfield, when Ælfeah Stybb and Brihtnoth, the son of Odda, attended the assembly at the request of the king: that every reeve should exact a pledge from his own shire, that they would all observe the decrees for the public security which King Æthelstan and his councillors had enacted, first at Grately, and afterwards at Exeter, and then at Faversham, and on a fourth occasion at Thundersfield, in the presence of the archbishop and all the bishops and the members of the royal council nominated by the king himself who were present; [and] that the decrees should be observed, which were established at this meeting, except those which had been abrogated; namely, the decrees relating to trading on Sunday and to bargaining outside a town in the presence of ample and trustworthy witnesses.

Tenthly: all the councillors all together gave their pledge to the archbishop at Thunderfield, when Ælfheah Stybb and Brihtnoth, Odda’s son, came to that assembly at the king’s command, that every reeve should receive the pledge in his own shire, that they would all maintain that peace as King Athelstan and his councillors had enacted it, first at Grately and again at Exeter, and afterwards at Faversham, and a fourth time at Thunderfield in the presence of the archbishop and all the bishops and his councillors, whom the king himself nominated, who were present; that the decrees which were established in this assembly should be observed, except those which had been repealed: namely Sunday marketing, and that one might with full and true witness buy outside a town.

Wahrscheinlich Königsthegn und identisch mit einem der zahlreichen miles und minister genannten Ælfheah unter 55 Urkk. a. 904—956, jedenfalls nicht (wie Schmid meinte) der Bischof von Winchester. Der Beiname kennzeichnet vielleicht die gedrungene Gestalt, war schwerlich schon Familienname. Ein Thegn Ælfheah ward 931 und 938 vom König mit Land beschenkt (Bi 682. 729); ein (anderer?) Ælfheah ward von K. Eadgar als Verwandter ausgezeichnet; Stevenson Crawford char. p. 84. Vgl. Gl Missus; Grafschaftsgericht 5a. 6a

Probably a king’s thegn and identical with one of the numerous Ælfheahs called miles and minister in 55 charters of a. 904—956; at any rate not (as Schmid thought) the bishop of Winchester. The by-name perhaps describes his stocky build; it was hardly a family name as yet. A thegn Ælfheah was granted land by the king in 931 and 938 (Bi 682. 729); a (different?) Ælfheah was distinguished by K. Eadgar as a kinsman; Stevenson Crawford char. p. 84. Cf. Gl Missus; Grafschaftsgericht 5a. 6a

Ein Beorhtnoð minister bezeugt 2 Urkk. a. 925—941 (Bi 648. 707), und war vielleicht Sohn jenes Odda, der a. 932—944 in 29 Urkk. zu oberst unter den Thegnas unterschreibt und identisch sein mag mit Odda, der an weniger vornehmer Stelle a. 904—941 zeugt

A Beorhtnoð minister witnesses 2 charters of a. 925—941 (Bi 648. 707), and was perhaps the son of that Odda who in a. 932—944 subscribes 29 charters at the head of the thegns and may be identical with the Odda who witnesses in a less distinguished position in a. 904—941
‘zum Gemot’ Schmid; allein die Missi stehen der Nationalversammlung gegenüber
‘to the gemot’ Schmid; but the missi stand over against the national assembly

‘Sheriff’ (s. d. Gl 9a) Schmid 597b; nicht sicher, da scir Bezirk allgemein heissen kann. Wenn auch dieser Amtsname noch nicht damals feststeht, mögen doch hauptsächlich solche gemeint sein, jedenfalls staatliche Beamte. Der Wortlaut dieser königlichen Verordnung scheint stückweise in c. 11 erhalten

‘Sheriff’ (see that word in Gl 9a) Schmid 597b; not certain, since scir can mean district in general. Even if this official title was not yet fixed at that time, such officers may nevertheless be chiefly meant, at any rate officials of the State. The wording of this royal ordinance seems to be preserved piecemeal in c. 11
‘zuerst östlich’ H, Price. Die Emendation ruht auf Q und prima vice IV As Pro. — Die Parenthese hinter ‘Greatley’ reicht besser bis ‘waren —’
‘first eastwards’ H, Price. The emendation rests on Q and prima vice IV As Pro. — The parenthesis after ‘Greatley’ would better extend as far as ‘were —’

Der König lädt zwar zum Reichstag, ernennt aber nicht zum Reichsversammlungsmitglied; vgl. mein National assembly S. 20. 47. Ernannt scheinen sie also als Kommission zur Abnahme des Eides auf die Gesetze; s. d. Gl 19. a

The king does indeed summon to the national assembly, but does not appoint members of it; cf. my National assembly p. 20. 47. They therefore seem to have been appointed as a commission to take the oath on the laws; see that word in Gl 19. a

These names are met with among the ministri regis (barons) who sign King Æthelstan’s charters; and two grants of land to Ælfeah Stybb are recorded in Birch, Cart. Sax. 648, 707. Odda is the name which usually comes first in the list of the ministri.
‘this meeting’ refers to the one first mentioned above, viz. Grately (II As.).
